reconcile.connective: Commentators read the demons' terrified confession as bare notional assent, not the heartfelt, obedient faith John's texts require for being born of God.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses this as a genuine contradiction: the demons meet 1 John's own confession test word for word, yet are plainly not 'of God.'

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Are those who believe that Jesus is the Christ 'of God'?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/of_god.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Are those who believe that Jesus is the Christ 'of God'?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: not that everyone that assents unto this, or preaches it, is born of God; a man may believe, and confess all this, as the devils themselves do, and yet be destitute of the grace of God; but the spirit, or doctrine, which contains these things in it, is certainly of God, or comes from him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill glosses 1 John 4:2's confession-test by explicitly excluding demons: assenting to and confessing the truth about Christ, as the devils do, does not make one born of God — the harmonization the contradiction needs.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Those who have only a notion of Christ - that he is the holy One of God, and have no faith in him, or love to him, go no further than the devil doth.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Commenting on the unclean spirit's confession in Mark 1:24, Henry contrasts a bare notional confession of Christ (what the devil manages) with the faith and love genuine believers have, denying the demon's words meet John's bar. Anchor block; sentence drawn from deep inside.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Another reason taken of an absurdity: If such a faith were the true faith whereby we are justified, the devils should be justified: for they have that, but yet notwithstanding they tremble, and are not justified therefore, neither is that faith a true faith.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The Geneva annotators argue by reductio on James 2:19: if the devils' bare assent were the justifying faith in view, the devils would be justified; since they are not, their assent is a different, lesser thing.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on 1 John 4:2
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact tension, distinguishing bare intellectual assent to the truths about Christ — the sort the devils themselves manage — from the confession that actually marks a man as born of God. (Used as the anchor because Haley's coverage of this specific passage could not be confirmed.)

link.note: Live apologetic treatment of James 2:19's demons-believe clause, drawing the same intellectual-assent-vs-saving-faith line the reconcile excerpts argue.
